name: Monthly site cost close, cost report and forecast at a remote underground gold mine
summary: Each month the site finance team closes the mine's books and tells head office what the month cost and what the year will cost. Accountants cut off payables, accrue goods received and contractor work not yet invoiced, value ore stockpiles and gold in the mill, split development between capital and operating cost, and produce cost per tonne and cost per ounce against budget. The site controller then walks the mine, mill and maintenance superintendents through their variances, writes the commentary, gets the general manager's sign-off and sends the report and an updated forecast to head office. Late receipts, contractor accruals that depend on superintendents on rotation, and the wait for the month's production numbers drive most of the adjustments and delay.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer with about 280 people at a remote northern Ontario site, a mid-market ERP, spreadsheets for metallurgical accounting and cost reporting, and a six-person site finance team.
baseline.notes: Describes 2019-2022 practice: close checklist and journals in the ERP, accrual and variance workbooks in spreadsheets, review meetings in person or by phone, report emailed to head office for quarterly consolidation.

trigger: The calendar month ends; payables and receiving are cut off on the last day and the close checklist starts on the first working day.
end_state: The site cost report signed by the general manager and the updated full-year forecast are with head office, and head office queries are answered.

volume.seasonality: Quarter-end months carry extra work: a full reforecast, inventory counts and head office's quarterly reporting deadlines; the year-end close in January is the longest.

evidence.note: One close per month by definition; matches the organisation file process_map entry.

systems.name: Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Payroll and timekeeping service (outsourced payroll with site time entry)

steps.name: Cut off payables and receipts
steps.description: On the first working days of the month the site accountants post the last invoices dated in the month, make sure warehouse receipts up to month end are entered, close the payables period in the ERP and run the open-PO and goods-received-not-invoiced reports.

error.defect_description: Late receipts or invoices for the month missed in the cut-off.

evidence.note: Three accountants working the cut-off together over the first working day or two; estimate.

steps.name: Accrue goods received not invoiced
steps.description: An accountant reviews the received-not-invoiced report, removes lines already invoiced or received in error, and prepares the accrual journal for the rest.

error.defect_description: Stale receipts accrued twice or never reversed.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Request contractor and service accruals
steps.description: The accountant emails each contract owner a list of their contractors with invoices received and asks for the value of work done in the month but not yet billed: drilling metres, open pit tonnes, shutdown crews, service calls.

evidence.note: Estimate; the organisation file names contractor accruals as a main driver of adjustments.

steps.name: Mine superintendent estimates contractor accruals
steps.description: The mine superintendent, or the mine captain on the other rotation, works out the open pit contractor's tonnes and the underground contractors' unbilled work from shift reports and contractor dailies and returns the estimates.

evidence.note: Estimate; the superintendent works field rotation in the organisation file.

steps.name: Maintenance superintendent estimates shutdown and repair accruals
steps.description: The maintenance superintendent lists contractor crews, outside repairs and rentals used in the month that have not been invoiced and estimates their value from timesheets and quotes.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Accrue payroll and bonuses
steps.description: The payroll administrator calculates wages, premiums and production bonus earned between the last pay period end and month end from the timesheets and bonus sheets, and gives the accrual to the accountant.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Post accruals and recurring journals
steps.description: The accountant posts the receipt, contractor and payroll accruals, reverses last month's, and posts recurring journals for power, insurance, camp catering, prepaid items, depreciation and royalties.

error.defect_description: Journal posted to the wrong cost centre or period.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile stores inventory and issues
steps.description: A second accountant reconciles the stores inventory ledger with the warehouse system, checks that issues are charged to the right department and work order, and books count adjustments and the obsolete stock provision.

error.defect_description: Issues charged to the wrong department.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: monthly inventory reconciliation

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Receive and check the production report
steps.description: The site controller receives the month's production report and mine-to-mill reconciliation: tonnes mined and milled, head grade, recovery, ounces poured and shipped, stockpile tonnes and gold in circuit. They check that the numbers tie between mine, mill and gold room.

evidence.note: Metallurgical balance and reconciliation are finalised a few days after month end in the organisation file's met accounting and reconciliation processes; wait is an estimate.

steps.name: Value stockpiles, gold in circuit and dore
steps.description: The controller applies the month's cost per tonne and per ounce to surface ore stockpiles, gold in circuit and dore on hand, compares the result with net realisable value at the current gold price and books the inventory adjustment.

error.defect_description: Stockpile tonnes or grade carried from the wrong survey.

control.basis: IFRS (IAS 2 Inventories) measurement at lower of cost and net realisable value, reviewed by the external auditor

evidence.note: Inventory of ore, gold in circuit and dore at the lower of cost and net realisable value is standard for gold producers reporting under IFRS; time is an estimate.

steps.name: Split development between capital and operating cost
steps.description: An accountant takes the metres of lateral development by heading from engineering, classifies each heading as capital (ramp, access) or operating (ore drives), and moves the matching labour, consumables and equipment cost to capital projects.

error.defect_description: Heading classified to the wrong capital project.

evidence.note: Gold producers report sustaining and growth capital separately from operating cost (wdo-guidance gives both for the reference mine); the per-metre allocation method is an estimate of common practice.

steps.name: Run preliminary cost report
steps.description: The controller runs the trial balance, refreshes the cost report workbook and calculates cost per tonne mined and milled, cost per ounce and all-in sustaining cost against budget and last month, and flags the departments with the largest variances.

evidence.note: The reference company guides and reports operating cost per ounce and all-in sustaining cost per ounce; time is an estimate.

steps.name: Mine superintendent reviews mine variances
steps.description: The controller sits down with the mine superintendent, or phones them on their days off, to go through mining costs by account: explosives, ground support, contractor and equipment costs, overtime. The superintendent explains real variances and points out miscoded charges.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Mill superintendent reviews mill variances
steps.description: The mill superintendent goes through reagents, grinding media, power and mill labour against budget and the tonnes milled and explains the differences.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Maintenance superintendent reviews maintenance variances
steps.description: The maintenance superintendent goes through parts, outside repairs, component rebuilds and contractor costs by fleet and plant area and explains large items.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Post corrections and reclassifications
steps.description: An accountant posts journals to move miscoded charges between departments and capital projects and to add accruals the superintendents identified, then reruns the report.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Write variance commentary and KPI package
steps.description: The controller writes the monthly commentary: costs against budget by department, cost per tonne and per ounce, capital spend by project, key one-offs and accrual risks, and assembles the KPI tables head office uses.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: General manager reviews and signs off
steps.description: The general manager reads the report, questions large variances and the forecast risks, and signs it off or sends it back for more explanation.

control.basis: Site general manager accountable for site cost reporting

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Send cost report to head office
steps.description: The controller emails the signed cost report, trial balance and supporting schedules to the corporate controller and uploads them to the consolidation folder.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Corporate controller reviews site report
steps.description: The corporate controller in Toronto reviews the site trial balance and cost report for consolidation, compares with prior months and guidance, and sends questions on accruals, inventory and capital classification.

evidence.note: Estimate; the organisation file sends the cost report to corporate financial reporting.

steps.name: Answer head office queries
steps.description: The controller researches and answers the corporate controller's questions, posts any late adjustments head office asks for in the still-open period, and resends the affected schedules and trial balance.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Update full-year forecast
steps.description: The controller rolls the forecast forward: actual months replace budget, the remaining months are adjusted for the latest mine plan tonnes and grade, known contractor and maintenance spend, gold price and exchange rate, and the full-year cost per ounce and capital are recalculated.

evidence.note: Monthly roll-forward with a fuller reforecast each quarter is an estimate of common practice; the organisation file says the forecast is updated for head office each month.

steps.name: General manager reviews quarterly reforecast
steps.description: At quarter end the general manager reviews the reforecast with the controller, checks the department heads' input on remaining spend and capital timing, and approves the numbers that go to head office for guidance.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Submit forecast to head office
steps.description: The controller sends the forecast workbook to head office for the corporate budget and guidance tracking and files the month's close binder.

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Corrections after variance review
exceptions.description: Superintendents find miscoded charges or missed accruals that are posted before the report goes out.

exceptions.name: GM sends report back
exceptions.description: The general manager asks for more explanation of variances or forecast risks.

exceptions.name: Head office queries
exceptions.description: The corporate controller questions accruals, inventory or capital classification.

exceptions.name: Quarter-end reforecast
exceptions.description: A fuller reforecast reviewed by the general manager at quarter end.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from running the trial balance to completed consolidated statements
benchmarks.population: APQC General Accounting Open Standards Benchmarking, about 2,300 organisations, cross-industry

evidence.note: The p50 is the APQC median. The p90 of 10 days is the published bottom-quartile threshold (10 days or more), used here as an approximate 90th percentile. The measure covers the whole company's consolidated close, not a site close plus forecast, so it is a reference rather than a like-for-like benchmark.

pain_points.description: Contractor accruals depend on superintendents on 14/14 rotation, so estimates arrive late and are often wrong, which shows up as next month's variances.

evidence.note: Organisation file names contractor accruals as the main driver of adjustments.

pain_points.description: The cost report waits for the metallurgical balance and reconciliation, which are themselves finalised days after month end.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Miscoded charges are found only in the variance meetings, forcing a second pass of journals and reruns.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Cost report, forecast and KPI tables live in linked spreadsheets refreshed by hand each month.

evidence.note: Estimate of 2019-2022 practice at single-mine producers.

sources.title: Metric of the Month: Cycle time for monthly close
sources.supports: APQC General Accounting benchmark (about 2,300 organisations): calendar days from running the trial balance to completed consolidated statements are 4.8 or fewer for the top quartile, 6.4 at the median and 10 or more for the bottom quartile.

sources.title: Wesdome Announces 2020 Fourth Quarter and Full Year Production Results; Provides 2021 Guidance
sources.supports: Eagle River complex 2021 guidance: 92,000-105,000 oz, operating cost C$900-1,000 per oz, AISC C$1,300-1,450 per oz, sustaining capital C$23-27 million and growth capital C$22-26 million; 2020 ore milled 236,297 t and production 90,278 oz.

assumptions: The organisation file gives this process no trigger. A monthly close starts on the calendar; this file records the payables cut-off (ap_ledger from site-ap) as the trigger and lists the other feeds, including the annual budget from corp-budget, as inputs.

The simulated cycle runs from month end to the forecast being submitted, so it is longer than the APQC trial-balance-to-statements measure; a median of about 8-10 days is consistent with a site report by working day 5-6 and the forecast a few days later.

Staffing: touch time per close is about 70 hours across all roles (about 0.5 FTE). Stated FTE are higher because cost accounting outside the close (daily coding questions, capital tracking, audit requests) is not stepped through.
Superintendents take part in accruals and variance review; the organisation file lists them on this process. The corporate controller is added as the head office reviewer (an existing role).
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file.
